title: From Software Developer to AI Engineer: Antje Barth
talk_summary: Antje Barth presents five steps for software developers becoming AI engineers, centered on learning model fundamentals, using AI dev tools like Amazon Q, prototyping with Bedrock, integrating agents, and staying current via community. The talk is largely an AWS product showcase (Amazon Q, Bedrock, Converse API, Bedrock Agents) with demos, not a technical deep-dive with measured results.

takeaways.what_they_do: Bedrock's Converse API standardizes parameters, system/user/assistant prompt roles, tool lists, and output format across different foundation models, with the platform translating to each model's native format.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can use the same parameters and bodies regardless of which model you choose and we are on the platform side we're handling this translation

takeaways.technique: Action groups with parameterized tool descriptions
takeaways.what_they_do: Bedrock Agents define tools as action groups where each action has a description (treated as prompt engineering) and required parameters the model must collect before invoking linked code.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the description here for Action to dig it's got some instructions again this is prompt engineering and then we've got some parameters that we can select collect

takeaways.what_they_do: Amazon Q /dev generates a step-by-step plan, then produces a diff change set the developer reviews before inserting code, rather than dumping code directly.
takeaways.evidence_quote: this isn't just a big shopping list of things that I need to do this is is actually a plan and it's a plan that Amazon Q can actually follow

takeaways.technique: Composed tool reasoning for multi-step tasks
takeaways.what_they_do: The Minecraft agent has no single 'come to me' tool; it reasons across get-player-location and move-to-location tools to solve the request.
takeaways.evidence_quote: there is no tool to come to us ... the agent's going to reason through a whole set of actions
